newsitem.title: UK: UK CBI says "disappointed" by base rate rise.
newsitem.headline: UK CBI says "disappointed" by base rate rise.

text.p: Britain's top employers group said on Friday it was disappointed by the new monetary policy committee's decision to raise base rates at its very first sitting.
The Confederation of British Industry's chief economist Kate Barker told BBC television she was "rather disappointed" by the rate rise.

"The central policy dilemma simply isn't going to go away," she said. "Consumer spending is likely to be pretty strong on the back of these very large windfall gains but exports are likely to continue to have a very tough time. We hope therefore that further rate rises can be kept to a minimum."
Economists now forecast windfall payouts from building societies converting into banks this summer could exceed 30 billion stg.
The Bank of England's new monetary policy committee met for the first time on Thursday and Friday and promptly raised rates by a quarter-point to 6.5 percent.

Barker said she hoped for fiscal tightening at the forthcoming budget despite Friday's rate rise. "We would still be looking for a small fiscal tightening in the budget, small tax rises to dampen down the consumer sector a little bit."
Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown will present his first budget on July 2.
